channel.title: English Radio
channel.description: English for the commute: stories in three parts, talks, vlogs, comedy, radio drama and music shows, with a different voice every time.
channel.itunes:author: English Radio

item.title: 1. Duchess Is Missing (1/3)
item.description: A three-part mystery in the Yorkshire Dales. Part 1 – the night a champion cow vanished, told by 14-year-old Ellie.

item.title: 2. Duchess Is Missing (2/3)
item.description: Part 2 – retired detective Agnes Pike takes the case. Boot prints, a goat who loves ginger biscuits, and a drone that saw something at two in the morning.

item.title: 3. Duchess Is Missing (3/3)
item.description: Part 3 – the thief tells his side of the story. An old farmhand, a goat, a long night by the beck, and the morning of the Thornby Show.

item.title: 4. Drive Time with Maya
item.description: A music show for the drive home. Maya plays six tracks made for this show – city pop, bossa nova, highlife, synthwave, swing and lo-fi – and tells the stories behind each sound.

item.title: 5. A Day on a Kiwi Dairy Farm (Vlog)
item.description: Sam runs a dairy farm in the Waikato, New Zealand. Come along from the 4 a.m. alarm to the last cow of the day – calves, a rotary shed, a cow in trouble, and a lot of mud.

item.title: 6. Planet Office
item.description: A nature documentary about the strangest habitat on Earth – the open-plan office. Watch the morning migration, the battle for the window desk, and the mystery of the missing yoghurt.

item.title: 7. Your Accent Is Not a Mistake (Talk)
item.description: A talk in the style of TED. Linguist Priya Raman explains why being understood matters more than sounding "native" – and why every accent tells a story.

item.title: 8. An Aussie in London (Stand-up)
item.description: Stand-up comedy. Australian comedian Nick Walsh explains what the British really mean when they say "not bad" – plus queues, tea, the weather, and a bowing contest in Tokyo.

item.title: 9. Voice Notes to Gran
item.description: Luke from Cape Town spends a year teaching English in a small mountain town in Japan. He sends voice messages to his grandmother. She sends them back. A year of rice fields, karaoke, snow – and family.

item.title: 10. Stories by the Fire
item.description: Uncle Femi tells three old West African folktales around the fire – how Anansi the spider bought all the world's stories, why the Sun and the Moon live in the sky, and the pot that held all the wisdom.

item.title: 11. Pole Pole (1/3)
item.description: A three-part story from northern Tanzania. Part 1 – agronomist Neema meets Haruto, a young engineer from Tokyo with three suitcases of sensors and an app that says it can predict the rain.

item.title: 12. Pole Pole (2/3)
item.description: Part 2 – Haruto tells his side. A model that was too confident, an apology to an old farmer, forty-five years of rain written in school exercise books, and a phone that buzzes at two in the morning.

item.title: 13. Pole Pole (3/3)
item.description: Part 3 – Mzee Joseph, the oldest farmer in Kisima, tells the end of the story. The night the river came, the real rains, and the young man the village named "child of the rain".
